Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 100, verses 1–11:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1} Allah, blessed and exalted, swears by the horses, because of the clear signs and manifest blessings in them that are known to creatures, and He swears by them in a state that no other kind of animal shares with them. So He says: {By the racers, panting}; that is, those that run with powerful, vigorous running from which comes the *dabh* (panting), which is the sound of their breath in their chests when their running becomes intense.

{2} {And strike sparks with their hooves}: by their hooves, striking the stones they tread upon, {striking sparks}; that is, fire is struck out from the hardness and strength of their hooves when they run.

{3} {And at dawn make raids}: against the enemies. This is a generally prevalent matter, that raids take place in the morning.

{4–5} {And raise thereby dust}; that is, by their running and raiding, {dust}, {and penetrate thereby into the midst of a host}; that is, with their riders they penetrate into the midst of the masses of the enemies whom they raided.

{6} The matter sworn to is His saying: {Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord}; that is, he withholds the good that Allah has upon him. The nature and disposition of man is that his soul does not permit what is owed of rights so that it fulfils them completely and abundantly; rather, its nature is laziness and withholding of financial and physical rights upon it, except for one whom Allah guides and who departs from this description to the description of generosity in discharging rights.

{7} {And indeed, he is witness to that}; that is, man, by what he knows of his own soul of withholding and ingratitude, is a witness to it, not denying it or rejecting it, because that [matter] is clear and evident. It is also possible that the pronoun refers back to Allah, [exalted]; that is, the servant is ungrateful to his Lord, and Allah is witness to that. In this is a warning and severe threat to the one who is ungrateful to his Lord, that Allah is witness against him.

{8} {And indeed, he is, in love of wealth, intense}; that is, he loves wealth very much, and this love is what caused him to abandon the obligatory rights upon him; he preferred the desire of his soul over the pleasure of his Lord. All of this is because he restricted his view to this abode and neglected the Hereafter.

{9–10} Therefore He says, urging him to fear the Day of the Threat: {Does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered}; that is, does this deluded one not know, {and what is within the breasts is obtained}; that is, Allah brings out the dead from their graves for their gathering and resurrection, and what is in the breasts, and what is hidden in the breasts of hidden good and evil, becomes manifest and apparent, so the secret becomes public and the inward becomes outward, and it appears on the faces of creatures as a result of their deeds.

{11} {Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully Acquainted with them}; that is, He is informed of their deeds, outward and inward, hidden and manifest, and He will recompense them for them. He specified His knowledge of them for that Day, although He is Acquainted with them at all times, because what is meant is the recompense for deeds that arises from Allah's knowledge and His awareness.

In this is a warning and severe threat to the one who is ungrateful to his Lord, that Allah is witness against him.

{8} {And indeed, he is, in love of wealth, intense}; that is, he loves wealth very much, and this love is what caused him to abandon the obligatory rights upon him; he preferred the desire of his soul over the pleasure of his Lord. All of this is because he restricted his view to this abode and neglected the Hereafter.

{9–10} Therefore He says, urging him to fear the Day of the Threat: {Does he not know that when the contents of the graves are scattered}; that is, does this deluded one not know, {and what is within the breasts is obtained}; that is, Allah brings out the dead from their graves for their gathering and resurrection, and what is in the breasts, and what is hidden in the breasts of hidden good and evil, becomes manifest and apparent, so the secret becomes public and the inward becomes outward, and it appears on the faces of creatures as a result of their deeds.

{11} {Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully Acquainted with them}; that is, He is informed of their deeds, outward and inward, hidden and manifest, and He will recompense them for them. He specified His knowledge of them for that Day, although He is Acquainted with them at all times, because what is meant is the recompense for deeds that arises from Allah's knowledge and His awareness.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 100, verses 1–11:

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

{1} Allah, blessed and exalted, swears by the horses, because of the clear signs and manifest blessings in them that are known to creatures, and He swears by them in a state that no other kind of animal shares with them. So He says: {By the racers, panting}; that is, those that run with powerful, vigorous running from which comes the *dabh* (panting), which is the sound of their breath in their chests when their running becomes intense.

{2} {And strike sparks with their hooves}: by their hooves, striking the stones they tread upon, {striking sparks}; that is, fire is struck out from the hardness and strength of their hooves when they run.

{3} {And at dawn make raids}: against the enemies. This is a generally prevalent matter, that raids take place in the morning.

{4–5} {And raise thereby dust}; that is, by their running and raiding, {dust}, {and penetrate thereby into the midst of a host}; that is, with their riders they penetrate into the midst of the masses of the enemies whom they raided.

{6} The matter sworn to is His saying: {Indeed, mankind is ungrateful to his Lord}; that is, he withholds the good that Allah has upon him. The nature and disposition of man is that his soul does not permit what is owed of rights so that it fulfils them completely and abundantly; rather, its nature is laziness and withholding of financial and physical rights upon it, except for one whom Allah guides and who departs from this description to the description of generosity in discharging rights.

{7} {And indeed, he is witness to that}; that is, man, by what he knows of his own soul of withholding and ingratitude, is a witness to it, not denying it or rejecting it, because that [matter] is clear and evident. It is also possible that the pronoun refers back to Allah, [exalted]; that is, the servant is ungrateful to his Lord, and Allah is witness to that. All of this is because he restricted his view to this abode and neglected the Hereafter.

{11} {Indeed, their Lord, that Day, is fully Acquainted with them}; that is, He is informed of their deeds, outward and inward, hidden and manifest, and He will recompense them for them.
